Governor Ivey Announces $1.8 Billion Niron Magnetics Investment

November 20, 2026

Press Releases

Share

DOTHAN –
 Governor Kay Ivey on Friday announced 
Niron Magnetics
, a global leader in the development and manufacturing of rare-earth-free Iron Nitride permanent magnets, will build a $1.8 billion advanced manufacturing campus in Dothan, Alabama. The 10,000-ton high-volume manufacturing plant is expected to create 700 high-wage jobs within five years.

“Alabama has demonstrated time and time again that when it comes to competing for the world’s most transformative industries, we are second to none,” 
said Governor Ivey.
 “Niron Magnetics’ $1.8 billion investment in Dothan is tremendous news for the Wiregrass and another significant win for Alabama’s growing manufacturing industry. We are proud to welcome Niron to Alabama and look forward to the opportunities this investment will create.”

Based in Minneapolis and founded in 2013, Niron Magnetics commercialized the world’s first high-performance permanent magnets that do not rely on rare earth elements. The Iron Nitride magnet technology uses abundant domestic materials to create a scalable, cost-competitive alternative to conventional neodymium-based magnets, supporting more resilient and domestic supply chains.

Niron will open its first high volume plant in 2027 in Sartell, Minnesota with a capacity of up to 1,500 tons of magnets annually. Alabama will be its second plant.

Niron’s magnets currently power applications across artificial intelligence infrastructure, automotive, industrial and consumer electronics. As the company scales manufacturing, its broader materials platform is creating new opportunities to develop the next generation of advanced solutions that power motion.

“Every step of the way, Alabama treated our success as its own,” 
said Niron Magnetics CEO Jonathan Rowntree.
 “We considered sites in 22 states, and Alabama stood out from the very first conversation.

“We’re grateful to Governor Ivey, the Alabama Department of Commerce and our local partners in Dothan and Houston County for their extraordinary work throughout the site selection process. We’re proud to call Alabama home to Niron’s high-volume manufacturing plant for rare-earth-free permanent magnets, and eager to grow alongside this community.”

With approximately 90 percent of global rare-earth magnet production concentrated overseas, Niron’s investment represents a significant opportunity to strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities and reduce supply chain vulnerabilities. The company’s technology is positioned to support several strategic U.S. industries, including automotive manufacturing, advanced technology and defense.

“Niron’s groundbreaking technology has the potential to make a lasting impact on industries that are critical to our nation’s future,” 
said Alabama Department of Commerce Secretary Ellen McNair.
 “Alabama is proud to welcome Niron Magnetics and looks forward to working alongside the company and our local partners as we turn this historic investment into opportunity for generations of Alabamians. This investment will create hundreds of high-quality career opportunities and bring new momentum to the Wiregrass region.”

The project represents a significant milestone in Alabama’s efforts to attract next-generation manufacturing and strengthen the domestic supply chains that support advanced manufacturing, automotive production and national security, McNair said. The investment will further position the state as a competitive destination for innovative industries and emerging technologies.

“This project means opportunity,” 
said Dothan Mayor Mark Saliba.
 “It means families can build their futures here with state-of-the-art technology that will strengthen America’s supply chain and our national security, which our country depends on. This is a transformational project. A company like Niron Magnetics elevates our whole city, region and state. New investment, new careers and new energy to our area economy. The technology built in Dothan, Alabama will power the future, and it will be built by the people of the Wiregrass.

“Our sincere thanks to Governor Kay Ivey and Niron Magnetics CEO Jonathan Rowntree for their support and vision in creating this opportunity for our area.”

Growing Alabama, SEEDS investment

The 1.6-million-square-foot campus at the Westgate Super Site industrial park will be Niron’s first high-volume manufacturing facility.

Creating the 446-acre Westgate Super Site was a multi-year effort by the city of Dothan, Houston County, the Industrial Development Board of the city of Dothan and the Dothan Area Chamber of Commerce to expand the Wiregrass region’s ability to compete for large-scale industrial projects.

State support for the Westgate Super Site has included strategic investments through both of Alabama’s primary industrial site development programs. In 2024, local partners received funding through the Site Evaluation and Economic Development Strategy program to support property acquisition and site development. The program helps communities prepare industrial properties that meet the requirements of high-impact economic development prospects.

The site subsequently received allocations through the Growing Alabama Tax Credit program, which leverages private investment to support improvements to publicly owned properties and expand the state’s inventory of development-ready industrial sites.

“The Westgate Super Site is a great example of what can be accomplished when state and local partners work together with a shared vision for economic growth,” 
continued Secretary McNair.
 “Through strategic investments from our SEEDS and Growing Alabama programs, we are helping communities across Alabama prepare sites that can compete for major industrial projects. Dothan, Houston County and their partners recognized the importance of making this investment in their community, and their efforts are creating new opportunities for the Wiregrass region.”

The site has access to a CSX rail line and earned 
CSX Select Site Platinum status in late 2025
.

Niron expects to begin construction in 2028, with production starting in 2029. 
Savills
 served as Niron’s advisor during the site selection process.

A photo from today’s announcement event is attached.
